events.title: Lebanese Republic Consolidates Post-Independence Institutions
events.note: The National Pact of 1943 description is accurate (Khoury + Riad al-Solh, unwritten power-sharing). The 1950 'consolidation' framing is plausible but too general to confirm or deny via web sources. Khoury presidency verified as running until 1952.

events.title: Beirut Emerges as Arab World's Financial and Commercial Hub
events.note: Beirut's role as Arab financial hub is historically well-attested but the specific 1950 date is too broad to verify as a discrete event. The banking secrecy law was 1956 (not 1950s general). Accurate description, year is notional.

events.title: Assassination of Prime Minister Riad Al-Solh
events.note: Confirmed: Riad al-Solh was killed on July 16-17, 1951 in Amman, Jordan by SSNP members in retaliation for the execution of Anton Saadeh. Details match.

events.title: Palestinian Refugees Settle in Lebanese Camps
events.note: Confirmed: UNRWA established camps including Shatila and Burj el-Barajneh following the 1948 war. Over 100,000 Palestinians fled to Lebanon. The 1951 framing is accurate for when camp infrastructure was established.

events.title: Rose Water Revolution: President Khoury Forced to Resign
events.note: Confirmed: Bechara El Khoury resigned September 1952 following general strike. Camille Chamoun elected successor on September 23, 1952. Army's refusal to suppress demonstrators confirmed.

events.title: Women's Suffrage Granted in Lebanon
events.note: Confirmed: A literacy-conditional law passed February 6, 1952; universal women's suffrage with amendment on February 18, 1953. Event year of 1953 is correct for universal suffrage. Lebanon was first Arab country to grant women full suffrage.

events.title: Lebanon Refuses to Join Baghdad Pact
events.note: Confirmed: Lebanon did not join the Baghdad Pact (1955). The event's framing of Nasserist pressure and the Christian-Muslim tension over Western alignment is historically well-documented.

events.title: Suez Crisis Deepens Lebanese Sectarian Polarization
events.note: Confirmed: Chamoun's refusal to break ties with Britain and France during Suez is documented in multiple sources on the 1958 crisis background. The Suez crisis (October 1956) and its Lebanese sectarian effect are well-attested.

events.title: Kataeb Party Strengthens Paramilitary Organization
events.note: Pierre Gemayel's Kataeb party and its paramilitary nature are documented, but the specific 1956 expansion claim is not distinctly verifiable. The general dynamic is accurate.

events.title: Rigged Parliamentary Elections Trigger Political Crisis
events.note: Confirmed: CIA funding for Chamoun-backed candidates documented (Wilbur Eveland memoir). Opposition claimed elections rigged. Elections held June 1957, result strongly pro-Chamoun.

events.title: Lebanese Civil Conflict and US Marine Intervention
events.note: Confirmed: Armed conflict erupted May 1958. US Marines landed July 15, 1958 (14,000-15,000 troops). Fuad Chehab elected president. Robert Murphy brokered compromise. US forces withdrew by October 1958. Casualty figure of ~2,000 is cited in sources.

events.title: Chehabism State-Building Reforms
events.note: Confirmed: Fuad Chehab launched modernization programs including Civil Service Council (1959), expanded infrastructure, and empowered military intelligence (Deuxieme Bureau). All details verified.

events.title: New Electoral Law Institutionalizes Confessional Quotas
events.note: Confirmed: Lebanon passed a new electoral law in 1960 restructuring constituencies. Confessional quotas embedded in Lebanese electoral law. This is a well-documented structural change.

events.title: Syrian Social Nationalist Party Coup Attempt Fails
events.note: Confirmed: SSNP attempted coup on December 31, 1961 (the last day of 1961, not 'in December'). Army suppressed it within hours. Hundreds arrested. Event year and details match.

events.title: Ba'ath Coups in Syria and Iraq Alarm Lebanon
events.note: Confirmed: Ba'athist coup in Iraq (February 1963) and Syria (March 8, 1963). Lebanese reaction of alarm documented. Category listed as 'bilateral_treaty' is wrong for this event but the event itself is accurate.

events.title: PLO Founded, Lebanese Territory Central to Palestinian Strategy
events.note: Confirmed: PLO founded June 2, 1964 following Arab League summit. Lebanon hosted largest Palestinian refugee population. The event details are accurate.

events.title: Fatah Launches First Armed Operations from Lebanese Territory
events.note: Confirmed: Fatah's first operation launched January 1, 1965. The attack targeted Israel's National Water Carrier. The description that it was launched 'from Lebanese territory' is the standard historical account, though the operational base was actually in Jordan/Syria. Date and event confirmed.

events.title: Banking Secrecy Law Cements Beirut as Arab Financial Safe Haven
events.note: YEAR ERROR: Lebanon's banking secrecy law was enacted on September 3, 1956, not 1965. The 1965 date in the event is wrong by 9 years. The description of the law's effect is accurate, but the year is incorrect.

events.title: Intra Bank Collapse and Banking Sector Reform
events.note: Confirmed: Intra Bank stopped payments October 14, 1966. Lebanon's largest bank at the time. Political rivals orchestrated institutional withdrawal of deposits. Led to banking regulation reforms. All details match.

events.title: Six-Day War Escalates Palestinian Armed Presence in Lebanon
events.note: Confirmed: June 1967 war sent Palestinian refugees to Lebanon and strengthened resistance movements. Lebanese authorities' inability to control fedayeen is well-documented.

events.title: Israeli Commando Raid on Beirut Airport
events.note: Confirmed: Israeli commando raid on December 28, 1968 destroyed Lebanese civilian aircraft. Event description says 'December 1968' which matches. Source confirms 13+ aircraft destroyed. All details accurate.

events.title: Lebanese Left Radicalizes After 1967 Defeat
events.note: Confirmed: Post-1967 radicalization of Lebanese left, Kamal Jumblatt's coalition-building, and the pre-civil war alignment structure are well-documented in sources on the Lebanese civil war.

events.title: Cairo Agreement Grants PLO Autonomous Military Presence
events.note: Confirmed: Cairo Agreement signed November 2-3, 1969. Brokered by Egyptian President Nasser. Granted PLO right to operate militarily in Lebanon and control Palestinian camps. All details match.

events.title: PLO Transfers Headquarters to Beirut After Black September
events.note: Confirmed: PLO expelled from Jordan in Black September 1970 (fighting September 16-27, 1970). Headquarters moved to Beirut. Lebanese became PLO's primary base until 1982. Details confirmed.

events.title: Palestinian Fedayeen Establish Control Over South Lebanon
events.note: Confirmed: By 1971 Palestinian fedayeen controlled large areas of southern Lebanon ('Fatahland'). Regular cross-border attacks and Israeli reprisals displacing Lebanese villagers are documented.

events.title: Final Pre-War Parliamentary Elections Held
events.note: Confirmed: 1972 parliamentary elections were the last before the civil war. The 1992 election sources explicitly describe it as 'first since 1972.' All details match.

events.title: Israeli Commando Raid Kills PLO Leaders in Beirut
events.note: Confirmed: Operation Spring of Youth on April 9-10, 1973. Three senior PLO leaders killed in Beirut apartments. Kamal Adwan, Kamal Nasser, and Muhammad Youssef al-Najjar. Lebanese army-PLO clashes followed. All details accurate.

events.title: Amal Movement Founded to Mobilize Shia Community
events.note: Confirmed: Harakat al-Mahrumin (Movement of the Disinherited) established by Musa al-Sadr in 1974. Military wing Amal formed January 20, 1975. The 1974 founding date and Shia mobilization mission are confirmed.

events.title: Sectarian Tensions Rise Over Power-Sharing Formula
events.note: Confirmed: By 1974 demographic tensions over the National Pact formula were at breaking point. Muslim demand for new census and revised power-sharing is documented as a direct cause of the civil war.

events.title: Lebanese Civil War Begins — Ain al-Rummaneh Massacre
events.note: Confirmed: Bus massacre April 13, 1975 in Ain al-Rummaneh, killing 27-30 Palestinians. Black Saturday massacres in December 1975 confirmed. Civil war ignition on April 13 is the canonical date.

events.title: Syria Intervenes in Lebanese Civil War
events.note: Confirmed: Syria sent troops June 1, 1976. Arab League legitimized as Arab Deterrent Force in October 1976 (40,000 troops). Intervention aimed at preventing PLO-leftist victory. All details match.

events.title: Tel al-Zaatar Palestinian Camp Massacre
events.note: Confirmed: Tel al-Zaatar siege began January 1976, massacre on August 12, 1976. Approximately 1,500 killed. Christian militias led by Kataeb. Camp in East Beirut. Death toll estimate of '1,500 to 3,000' in event is slightly high; Wikipedia gives ~1,500, but range is cited elsewhere.

events.title: Kamal Jumblatt Assassinated, Lebanese Forces Consolidate
events.note: Confirmed: Jumblatt assassinated March 16, 1977. Syria widely blamed. Lebanese Forces consolidation and Frangieh family clash (Ehden massacre, June 1978) also documented. Note: Frangieh clash was 1978, not concurrent with Jumblatt assassination in 1977, but both occurred under Gemayel's consolidation drive.

events.title: Israeli Operation Litani Invades South Lebanon and UNIFIL Deployed
events.note: Confirmed: Operation Litani launched March 14, 1978 with ~25,000 troops. ~300,000 displaced. UN Resolution 425 passed March 19, 1978, establishing UNIFIL. Withdrawal by June 1978. All details match.

events.title: Imam Musa al-Sadr Disappears in Libya
events.note: Confirmed: Musa al-Sadr disappeared August 31, 1978 during visit to Libya. Widely believed killed on Gaddafi's orders. Became martyr figure for Amal and later Hezbollah. All details confirmed.

events.title: Islamic Revolution in Iran Inspires Lebanese Shia
events.note: Confirmed: Iranian Revolution of 1979 directly inspired Lebanese Shia movements. Iran's subsequent support for Hezbollah following 1982 invasion is documented. Event is accurate.

events.title: Kataeb Destroys Tigers Militia, Consolidates Christian Military
events.note: Confirmed: Safra massacre (Day of the Long Knives) occurred July 7, 1980. Bashir Gemayel's forces attacked National Liberal Party Tigers at Safra beach resort. Lebanese Forces officially unified by November 22, 1980. All details match.

events.title: Syrian Missile Crisis and Israeli-Syrian Confrontation in Lebanon
events.note: Confirmed: April 1981 Israeli aircraft downed Syrian helicopters over Bekaa; Syria deployed SAMs. Philip Habib brokered ceasefire. July 1981 PLO-Israel ceasefire also brokered by Habib. All details confirmed.

events.title: Israel Invades Lebanon — Operation Peace for Galilee
events.note: Confirmed: Israel invaded June 6, 1982. Bashir Gemayel elected president August 23, 1982, assassinated September 14, 1982 by SSNP operative. All details match. Note: 76,000 troops figure is consistent with sources.

events.title: Sabra and Shatila Massacre
events.note: Confirmed: Massacre September 16-18, 1982. Kataeb/Lebanese Forces entered camps in Israeli-controlled West Beirut. 800-3,500 killed. Kahan Commission found Sharon bore personal responsibility. All details match.

events.title: US Embassy and Marine Barracks Bombings Force Western Withdrawal
events.note: Confirmed: US Embassy bombing April 1983 killed 63. Marine barracks October 23, 1983: 241 Americans killed (220 Marines + 18 Navy + 3 Army). French barracks: 58 paratroopers killed. Western forces withdrew February 1984. All details match.

events.title: May 17 Agreement with Israel Collapses Under Syrian Pressure
events.note: Confirmed: Agreement signed May 17, 1983. Lebanon abrogated it on March 5, 1984 under Syrian pressure. Syria organized internal opposition and refused to withdraw troops. All details confirmed.

events.title: West Beirut Falls to Amal and PSP Militias
events.note: Confirmed: After US Marine departure in February 1984, Amal and Druze PSP militias took control of West Beirut. Green Line dividing capital confirmed for this period.

events.title: Israeli Partial Withdrawal Creates Security Zone, War of the Camps Begins
events.note: Confirmed: Israel withdrew most forces 1985, retaining Security Zone. Amal backed by Syria besieged Palestinian camps (War of the Camps 1985-1988). Hezbollah emerged as primary resistance. All details match.

events.title: Hezbollah Consolidates as Political-Military Organization
events.note: Confirmed: Hezbollah founded 1982 with IRGC support, consolidated in Bekaa Valley and south Lebanon 1985 (year of its official manifesto). Social services + resistance ideology + Khomeini doctrine all confirmed.

events.title: Lebanese Economy Collapses, Currency Hyperinflation
events.note: Confirmed: Lebanese pound collapsed during civil war. The 1986-1987 hyperinflation peak is consistent with documented currency history. Diaspora remittances, drug cultivation in Bekaa, and militia economics are documented.

events.title: Western Hostage Crisis Peaks in Beirut
events.note: Confirmed: Iran-Contra affair in 1986-1987 linked to hostage releases. Islamic Jihad held dozens of Western hostages. Multiple sources confirm this crisis peaked mid-1980s.

events.title: Prime Minister Rashid Karami Assassinated
events.note: Confirmed: Karami killed June 1, 1987 by bomb in his Puma helicopter. Attributed to Lebanese Forces. Samir Geagea later convicted. Details match.

events.title: Constitutional Vacuum: Competing Governments Formed
events.note: Confirmed: Amine Gemayel's term expired September 22, 1988 without successor. Gemayel appointed Aoun as interim PM. Two competing governments (Aoun in East Beirut, Hoss in West Beirut). All details confirmed.

events.title: General Aoun's War of Liberation and Taif Accord
events.note: Confirmed: Aoun declared War of Liberation against Syria March 1989. Taif Agreement signed October 22, 1989, ratified November 5, 1989 in Taif, Saudi Arabia. Equal 50-50 Christian-Muslim parliamentary representation confirmed. Syrian withdrawal provision confirmed.

events.title: Aoun Defeated; Lebanese Civil War Formally Ends
events.note: Confirmed: Syrian forces defeated Aoun October 13, 1990. Aoun fled to French embassy and went into exile. Civil war conventionally ends October 1990. ~150,000 dead and ~1 million displaced confirmed.

events.title: Lebanese Militias Disarmed — Except Hezbollah
events.note: Confirmed: Post-Taif militia dissolution in 1991. Hezbollah explicitly exempted as 'resistance movement' against Israeli occupation. This exception is a well-documented and consequential decision.

events.title: Syria Signs Brotherhood and Cooperation Treaty with Lebanon
events.note: Confirmed: Treaty of Brotherhood, Cooperation and Coordination signed May 22, 1991 (some sources say May 23). By Presidents Assad and Hrawi. Defense agreement followed September 1, 1991. All details match.

events.title: First Post-War Parliamentary Elections and Hariri Reconstruction Era
events.note: Confirmed: Elections held August-October 1992, first since 1972. Conducted under Syrian tutelage. Christian boycott documented. Rafik Hariri appointed PM and launched Solidere reconstruction. All details match.

events.title: Israel Launches Operation Accountability Against Hezbollah
events.note: Confirmed: Operation Accountability launched July 25, 1993. Week-long campaign. 300,000-400,000 civilians displaced northward. US-brokered July Understanding (oral ceasefire). All details match.

events.title: South Lebanon Army Maintains Israeli-Backed Border Strip
events.note: Confirmed: SLA controlled Israeli Security Zone. Khiam detention center documented. Continuous low-level war with Hezbollah. SLA collapse in 2000 confirmed.

events.title: Lebanese Forces Leader Geagea Jailed in Politically Motivated Trial
events.note: Confirmed: Geagea arrested April 21, 1994. Life sentence. Widely seen as politically motivated by Syrian-backed order. Pardoned July 2005 after Syrian withdrawal. Only militia leader prosecuted post-amnesty. All details match.

events.title: Constitutional Amendment Extends President's Term Under Syrian Pressure
events.note: Confirmed: Constitutional amendment October 19, 1995 extended Hrawi's term three years to November 1998. Syrian intelligence chief Ghazi Kan'an instructed deputies to vote for it. All details match.

events.title: Hariri's Economic Strategy Deepens Public Debt
events.note: Confirmed: Hariri's reconstruction strategy and resulting public debt growth are documented. Critics about disproportionate benefit to his business interests are on record. By 1997 debt was crisis-level.

events.title: Israel Launches Operation Grapes of Wrath, Qana Massacre
events.note: Confirmed: Operation Grapes of Wrath April 1996, 16-day campaign. Qana massacre April 18, 1996: 106 killed at UNIFIL compound (not 154 total civilian deaths as in event — total Lebanese civilian deaths were 154 across the whole operation). Hezbollah parliamentary participation in 1996 elections confirmed.

events.title: Ansariyya Ambush Kills Twelve Israeli Commandos
events.note: Confirmed: Ansariya ambush September 4, 1997. Twelve Israeli Shayetet 13 naval commandos killed. Hezbollah intercept of Israeli communications key to ambush. All details match.

events.title: Syrian-Backed Emile Lahoud Elected President
events.note: Confirmed: Lahoud elected president November 1998 in a landslide (118 out of 118 attending MPs). Constitution amended to allow army commander to run. Syrian backing well-documented. Hariri resigned as PM. All details match.

events.title: Israeli PM Barak Announces Intention to Withdraw from South Lebanon
events.note: Confirmed: Ehud Barak won 1999 election on pledge to withdraw from Lebanon within one year. Announcement and subsequent execution of withdrawal in May 2000 confirmed.

events.title: Israel Withdraws from South Lebanon; Hezbollah Claims Victory
events.note: Confirmed: Israel withdrew May 24-25, 2000. SLA immediately collapsed. Hezbollah claimed historic victory. 22-year occupation ended. All details match.

events.title: Kornet Shehwan Declaration Calls for Syrian Withdrawal
events.note: Confirmed: The Kornet Shehwan Gathering (named after the Beirut suburb) issued its declaration in April 2001 calling for Syrian withdrawal. Syrian harassment of signatories documented.

events.title: Shebaa Farms Dispute Preserves Hezbollah's Resistance Justification
events.note: Confirmed: Shebaa Farms dispute well-documented post-2000 as Hezbollah's stated justification for maintaining armed resistance. UN position that area is Syrian territory is documented.

events.title: Syrian Presence Increasingly Resented Across Confessional Lines
events.note: Confirmed: By 2003 cross-confessional resentment of Syrian occupation was growing. Iraqi War fears about tightening Syrian grip are documented in contemporary accounts.

events.title: UN Resolution 1559 Demands Syrian Withdrawal and Militia Disarmament
events.note: Confirmed: UNSCR 1559 passed September 2, 2004. Demanded Syrian withdrawal, free elections, militia disarmament. Lahoud term extension was the trigger. Hariri publicly opposed. All details match.

events.title: Rafik Hariri Assassinated; Cedar Revolution Forces Syrian Withdrawal
events.note: Confirmed: Hariri killed February 14, 2005, killing him and 21 others (event says 21, Wikipedia says 21 others + Hariri = 22 total). Cedar Revolution culminated in 1-1.5 million in Martyrs' Square March 14. Syria withdrew by April 26-27, 2005 (29-year presence). All details match.

events.title: Michel Aoun Returns, Signs Alliance with Hezbollah
events.note: Confirmed: Aoun returned from 15 years in France on May 7, 2005. MOU with Hezbollah signed February 6, 2006 (not 2005 as implied). The alliance is confirmed. Minor: MOU was 2006 not 2005, but the return and the process started in 2005.

events.title: Israel-Hezbollah Thirty-Three Day War
events.note: Confirmed: Hezbollah captured two soldiers July 12, 2006. War lasted 33 days. ~1,200 Lebanese killed (sources vary between 1,100-1,200). $3.6 billion in damage. ~1 million displaced. UN Resolution 1701 ended fighting. All details match.

events.title: Nahr al-Bared Camp Destroyed in Siege Against Fatah al-Islam
events.note: Confirmed: Battle May-September 2, 2007. ~400+ killed. Camp destroyed. ~30,000 Palestinians displaced. Lebanese army's largest post-civil war operation. All details match.

events.title: Serial Assassinations Target Anti-Syrian Politicians; STL Established
events.note: Confirmed: Series of assassinations targeting anti-Syrian politicians in 2007. STL established by UNSCR 1757 on May 30, 2007 via Chapter VII after parliament failed to ratify. All details match.

events.title: Hezbollah Seizes West Beirut; Doha Agreement Grants Veto Power
events.note: Confirmed: May 2008 Hezbollah seized West Beirut after government moved against its telecom network. 80+ killed. Doha Agreement gave Hezbollah/allies 11 ministerial posts (blocking minority). Michel Suleiman elected president May 25, 2008. All details match.

events.title: March 14 Alliance Wins Parliamentary Elections
events.note: Confirmed: March 14 won June 7, 2009 elections with 71 seats. March 8 won 57 seats. Saad Hariri took months to form unity government including Hezbollah ministers. All details match.

events.title: Special Tribunal for Lebanon Moves Toward Hezbollah Indictments
events.note: Confirmed: STL began work 2009-2010. Leaks about Hezbollah indictments created political crisis. Hezbollah declared tribunal politically motivated. Confirmed as major 2010 fault line.

events.title: Hezbollah Topples Hariri Government, Syrian War Spills into Lebanon
events.note: Confirmed: Opposition resigned January 12, 2011 toppling Hariri government. Najib Mikati formed next government with Hezbollah backing. Syrian civil war began March 2011. All details match.

events.title: Syrian Refugee Crisis Begins — Lebanon Hosts Highest Per-Capita Burden
events.note: Confirmed: Syrian refugees began entering Lebanon in large numbers from 2011. 1.5+ million refugees documented. Lebanon confirmed as country with highest per-capita refugee burden globally. All details match.

events.title: Syrian War Spills into Tripoli and Border Areas
events.note: Confirmed: Fierce fighting in Tripoli between Sunni Bab al-Tabbaneh and Alawite Jabal Mohsen 2012. Cross-border Hezbollah-rebel battles in Bekaa. Government dissociation policy confirmed.

events.title: Hezbollah Expands Precision Missile Arsenal
events.note: Hezbollah's missile arsenal expansion is generally documented but the specific 2012 focus and '50,000 rockets' figure for 2012 cannot be confirmed precisely via web search. The general trend is accurate but the specific year and figure are not distinctly verifiable.

events.title: Hezbollah Openly Joins Syrian War; Car Bombs Strike Beirut
events.note: Confirmed: Nasrallah publicly declared Hezbollah involvement in Syria in May 2013. Car bombings in southern Beirut (Dahiyeh) and Tripoli confirmed throughout 2013. August 15, 2013 bombing killed 27. All details match.

events.title: Presidential Vacuum Begins; ISIS Seizes Arsal
events.note: Confirmed: Presidential vacuum began May 2014 when Suleiman's term expired. Battle of Arsal August 2-7, 2014 against ISIS/Nusra. Fragile truce established. Hostages held for years confirmed. All details match.

events.title: You Stink Protests Expose Cross-Sectarian Civic Anger
events.note: Confirmed: Garbage crisis triggered 'You Stink' movement summer 2015. Cross-confessional protests. Garbage remained unresolved with waste burned. All details match.

events.title: Michel Aoun Elected President After 29-Month Vacuum
events.note: Confirmed: Aoun elected president October 31, 2016 ending 29-month vacancy (since May 2014). Saad Hariri became prime minister. 83 MPs voted for Aoun. All details match.

events.title: Saad Hariri's Forced Resignation from Saudi Arabia
events.note: Confirmed: Hariri resigned from Riyadh November 4, 2017. Macron intervened diplomatically. Hariri returned to Lebanon and suspended then rescinded resignation December 5, 2017. All details match.

events.title: Lebanese Army Defeats ISIS on Syrian Border
events.note: Confirmed: Lebanese army Operation 'Dawn of the Outskirts' launched August 20, 2017. Operation ended August 30, 2017. ISIS expelled from Ras Baalbek-Qaa border area within ~10 days (event says 'a week' — slightly compressed but directionally correct).

events.title: Hezbollah Bloc Wins Parliamentary Majority; CEDRE Aid Conditioned on Reform
events.note: Confirmed: May 6, 2018 elections. Hezbollah and allies won 68 seats (simple majority). CEDRE conference held April 6, 2018 in Paris pledged ~$11 billion in soft loans. Reform conditions for privatization/public sector. All details match.

events.title: October Revolution and Eruption of Financial Crisis
events.note: Confirmed: October 17, 2019 protests triggered by WhatsApp tax. Slogan 'killun yaani killun' (all of them means all of them) confirmed. Largest protests in Lebanese history. Simultaneous financial crisis, capital controls, pound devaluation all confirmed.

events.title: Beirut Port Explosion Devastates Capital
events.note: Confirmed: August 4, 2020. 2,750 tonnes of ammonium nitrate. 218 dead. 7,000 injured. 300,000 displaced. One of largest non-nuclear explosions in history. PM Diab's government resigned six days later. All details match.

events.title: Lebanese Pound Collapses, Hyperinflation Begins
events.note: Confirmed: Pound lost 80%+ in 2020. Triple-digit inflation. World Bank described as one of worst financial collapses in modern history. Banks denied depositors dollar savings. All details match.

events.title: COVID-19 Compounds Lebanon's Crises
events.note: Confirmed: COVID-19 struck Lebanon in early 2020. Healthcare system overwhelmed by simultaneous financial crisis and port explosion. Unprecedented humanitarian emergency. All details match.

events.title: State Infrastructure Collapses: Electricity, Fuel, and Judiciary
events.note: Confirmed: Electricity provision down to 1-2 hours/day in 2021. Fuel shortages. Judge Tarek Bitar's port explosion investigation repeatedly suspended by Hezbollah and Amal legal maneuvers. All details confirmed.

events.title: Parliamentary Elections Produce Fragmented Result; Presidential Vacuum Returns
events.note: Confirmed: Elections May 15, 2022. Hezbollah/Amal lost majority (58 seats). 13 independent reformers won seats. Aoun's term expired October 2022 without successor — new presidential vacuum. All details match.

events.title: Lebanon-Israel Maritime Border Agreement
events.note: Confirmed: Agreement signed October 27, 2022. US-brokered (Amos Hochstein). Resolved offshore gas field dispute (Karish to Israel, Qana to Lebanon). Lebanon does not formally recognize Israel making direct negotiation impossible — confirmed. Hezbollah tacit acceptance documented.

events.title: IMF Negotiations Stall; Depositor Protests Target Banks
events.note: Confirmed: IMF negotiations stalled 2023. Political class refused banking sector reform. Riad Salameh faced European embezzlement charges (confirmed). Armed bank hold-ups by depositors to withdraw own savings documented. All details match.

events.title: Hezbollah-Israel Border War of Attrition Begins
events.note: Confirmed: Following Hamas October 7 attack, Hezbollah began exchanging fire with Israel in 'war of solidarity.' Drones, anti-tank missiles, Israeli strikes in south Lebanon. Tens of thousands displaced both sides throughout 2023.

events.title: Israel-Hezbollah War: Leadership Decimated; Ceasefire Reached
events.note: Confirmed: Nasrallah assassinated September 27, 2024 in Israeli airstrike on Dahieh. Entire top leadership including Ali Karaki and others killed. Ground operations in south Lebanon. US-brokered ceasefire November 2024. Lebanese army deployment south confirmed. All details match.

events.title: Joseph Aoun Elected President; New Government Formed
events.note: Confirmed: Army commander Joseph Aoun elected president January 9, 2025 (99 votes). Nawaf Salam (former ICJ judge and UN ambassador) appointed PM January 13, 2025, formed government February 8, 2025. US and Saudi backing documented. All details match.

events.title: Post-War Recovery and International Reconstruction Engagement
events.note: Event describes 2025 trajectory accurately based on early 2025 context (new president, reformist PM, weakened Hezbollah, donors conditioning reconstruction). However this is a forward-looking/ongoing narrative as of 2025 and cannot be distinctly verified as a completed discrete event.
